Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test failure is related to an XPath query returning null where it should return a node or attribute value based on the XML context. The relevant test calls assertXPathNodeType(context, "//vendor", Element.class), which internally calls JXPathContext.getPointer(xpath) to obtain a Pointer to the node matching the XPath. The current bug report describes that descendant or self axes do not work correctly at the root node in XPath queries; for example, the query "//root/@id/text()" returns null when accessing the root itself.

In examining the code, JXPathContext.getPointer(String) delegates to getPointer(String, Expression) which gets the pointer by computing the value of the compiled XPath expression on an evaluation context. If the result is an EvalContext, it returns the single node pointer from that EvalContext. But crucially, if the result is a NodePointer (the Pointer implementation), it checks if the pointer is actual (exists) and throws an exception if not.

The problem likely lies in either the evaluation of descendant-or-self axes expressions at the root or in the NodePointer's isActual() method implementation. The XPath expression "//root/@id/text()" relies on the descendant-or-self axis starting from the root node to find the attribute's text node. If the NodePointer to the root or attribute node incorrectly returns false from isActual(), getPointer throws JXPathNotFoundException or returns null.

The recent bug report confirms this issue with descendant-or-self axes usage on the root node. Thus, the fault is primarily in the model handling the root node descendants, specifically in how node existence is detected or how the XPath evaluation treats the root context node for descendant or self axis queries.

The failing test reflects this by requesting a node via such an XPath and expecting a non-null Element node. The failure strongly indicates that the evaluation context or NodePointer for the JDOM model does not properly include the root node or its attributes in descendant-or-self axes queries, resulting in null pointers and test failures.

Hence the root cause: The XPath descendant or self axis is not correctly evaluated on the root node in the JXPath JDOM model, causing queries like "//root/@id/text()" or "//vendor" to not find the expected nodes because the nodes are either missing or marked as non-actual in the evaluation, resulting in null returns where nodes are expected.

This diagnosis is supported by the current bug report and behavior of the pointer evaluation logic in getPointer.

Suggested areas to investigate or fix include the NodePointer's handling of root node existence and the XPath expression evaluation regarding descendant-or-self axes at the root node.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
